reasoning: Taa marbuta after ن is e, so sane, not MSA sana. Everyday Ramallah word for year.
Everyday word, so ق is a glottal stop. Taa marbuta after م is e. Used exactly as fate or what God allotted, often in 'isme w naSiib.
Said as one run-together phrase, il-7amdilla, with the linking kasra and a geminate l into Allaah. No MSA case ending -u in speech.
Palestinian keef, not MSA kayfa. ج behaves as a sun letter in Levantine, so il- assimilates to ij-. The question mark is not romanized.
Form VI takes the colloquial it- prefix, itfaaja', not MSA tafaaja'a. Final hamza is a glottal stop. Palestinians also say inSadam for a stronger shock.
Long ii, not ee. Standard word for a bag; kiis naylon is the plastic one.
Form II with shadda on ك, so the k doubles. Everyday verb for concentrating or paying attention.
Sun letter س assimilates the article. The frozen -u linker survives in this formula, but the diphthong does not: Palestinians say 3aleekum, so the ي carries kasra.
ض is emphatic D. Taa marbuta after ر is a. An MSA-origin word Palestinians genuinely use in conversation.
The short vowel drops, giving the initial cluster rfii', and ق is a glottal stop. Means companion or mate; Sadii' is the commoner word for friend.
Masculine imperative with the dropped first vowel, tkhayyal. إنو is innu with shadda on ن and a final oo.

reasoning: shoob is dry scorching heat, not humidity. Muggy would be ij-jaw ruTuube or ij-jaw mkhannee'.
reet has the long ee, written with kasra on the ي. The b- present prefix gives ba'dar, with ق as a glottal stop.
بلش is form II ballash with shadda. ما negates the verb, and wi'if has a glottal ق plus the helping vowel between ق and ف.
The final cluster is broken by a helping vowel, khubiz, not MSA khubz.
illi is the relative pronoun; fhimtu is I understood it, with the object -u. Hyphenating the article is not needed since illi is not il- plus a noun.
3indi for I have. maw3id keeps the aw diphthong before the w, as Palestinians say it.
The conjunction is a bare w before a consonant. ط is emphatic T.
Word-initial hamza seat is just the vowel i. The country name is borrowed with long uu and ii; stress and exact vowel length vary between speakers.
ض is emphatic D. An MSA-shaped adjective that is nonetheless said in Ramallah; for an everyday mess a speaker is as likely to say mkharbaT.
ق in wa't is a glottal stop. ف is a moon letter so the article stays il-.
il-mafrooD plus kaan is the usual way to say was supposed to. The bare subjunctive yikhlaS follows, with no b- prefix.
ث is realised as t in urban Palestinian, so the spelling is respelled ثلاجة to تلاجة. Shadda on ل, and taa marbuta after ج is e.
Medial hamza is a glottal stop, written '. This is a learned borrowing, so most Ramallah speakers keep the ث as th rather than shifting it to t.
The final cluster takes a helping vowel in isolation, nahir; in a construct such as nahr il-urdun it stays nahr.
